September 2026 (2026-09-01 to 2026-09-30), all shifts. Window coverage: complete.
Contribution margin not set: without an owner margin no lost contribution is priced, so the dollars are paper and machine time.

Two speeds, never one definition: the speed lever is each grade's trailing-year baseline (targets.json), and the required speed, 675 ft/min at 10% downtime (rates.json, the post), converts machine minutes to MSF not made and is no lever. This window ran 598.5 ft/min with stops, against neither.
The supervisor lens: the controllable levers ranked, each its gap to its band; side trim is schedule-driven and listed after with the rows shown apart.

Each lever is its gap to its band in targets.json, summed over the shifts of the window: a shift inside its band adds nothing, and the cost inside the bands is shown apart, at standard, outside the total.
A yearly figure is this period's rate, period-to-date dollars per production day x the post's production days a year, never a shift's or a day's own.
For all shifts it is each shift's period-to-date rate added up, so the shifts' yearly figures add to it.
These name where to look and whom to ask; they never prescribe a machine adjustment.

Whole dollars that add up: each shift of each production day prints its nearest dollar, its lines sharing it by the largest remainder, and every day, window and line is its shifts' whole dollars added up.

Over several days these whole dollars, added shift by shift, can read off the same quantities priced at once in cents, which the formulas and receipts state: at the post's rates by under thirteen dollars over the whole record.
How a dollar is priced, for Speed under the grade baseline: 683.58 min x $1,200/hr machine time = $13,671.60; contribution: margin not set. It prints $13,669 (whole dollars that add up).

Rates: paper $55/MSF (post), machine time $1,200/hr (post), contribution margin not set (assumption: owner to set), trim target 3% (owner, 2026-11-10). Dollars are synthetic records priced at assumed rates (the post's defaults unless changed); they are not a real plant's figures.
Where to look
- The downtime minutes by reason → “Which downtime reason cost the most minutes this month?”
- Side trim, shear and each dry-end reason → “Waste breakdown this month”
- Each grade and web width against its best-fifth speed → “Where is the speed opportunity this month?”
